summary: 77/193 belongs to III.1, dressing another person.

summary: LB 291 is a negative command expressed by Infectum, not bare Imperativ.

summary: Assign the command to dress someone to sense 1
rationale: The example says 'zieht ihm diese Kleider an', confirmed by 77/193. Dressing another person belongs to existing sense 1 ('bekleiden ... anziehen lassen'), rather than sense 2 ('anziehen, tragen').

summary: New box Nomen Actionis: example for sense 1 in Nomen Actionis (JTM 1.3/27)

data.translation: Wenn der Vorgang des Ankleidens und das alles vorbei ist, dann bitten sie um die Erlaubnis der Eltern

data.translation: Dann beginnt das Bekleiden (des Bräutigams), es kommen der Trauzeuge und der Priester, und der Priester segnet die Kleider des Bräutigams und bekleidet ihn damit.

summary: New box ko-Preterit: example for sense 1 in ko-Preterit (Jan 2.31/4859)

summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (Jan 2.26/4435)

summary: New sense 2: (mit xəd) durch Zauber eine Gestalt annehmen, sich verwandeln

summary: New idiom: lwəšle/lowəš ǧasad 'Fleisch annehmen, Mensch werden'

data.translation: Er ist das Wort aus dem Munde Gottes, das Fleisch und Sohn Gottes geworden ist und hat uns gerettet

rationale: Single theological collocation; not already listed as an idiom in the supplied entry or ǧasad search. The phrase preserves the clothing metaphor lost in German.

summary: New idiom: lwəšle/lowəš dayroyuṯo 'das Mönchsgewand anlegen, ins Mönchsleben eintreten'

data.headword: lwəšle/lowəš dayroyuṯo 'das Mönchsgewand anlegen, ins Mönchsleben eintreten'
data.turoyo: Maḥətle əšme Yuḥanun. Šləḥle aǧ ǧule di ʕarabiye w lwəšle dayroyuṯo, ʕbədle šet w ʕəsri əšne tamo.
data.translation: He took the name Yuhannun. He took off the Arab clothes and put on the monastic habit; he spent twenty-six years there.

rationale: Abstract monastic-life noun as garment/status object with renaming and prolonged residence. dayroyuṯo lookup found only rsm ordination, no existing lwš phrase; single clear context.

summary: Routine counts support 214 additional routine uses: I Preterit 109 and Infectum 42, III Preterit 31 and Infectum 10, with smaller other cells. They do not require occurrence decisions and were not reconstructed as verse evidence.
The inherited I and III Detransitive sections had examples but no numbered gloss. Proposed Detransitive sense 1 makes those existing meanings explicit; active numbering stays unchanged.

Classified article-bearing lwošo and təlwišo as Nomen Actionis, provisionally. The supplied noun syntax and event meaning do not prove the reader's Detransitive Infinitiv labels; editorial paradigm confirmation is required.
The theological phrase was searched as ǧasad; it is incidentally quoted under xlṣ but is not listed as an idiom under lwš. Searches for nabuniye and təlwišo found no existing phrase.

I and III distinguish wearer-oriented putting on from dressing another person, but suffixes and subject continuity must be checked. III.2 has a clear self-dressing Preterit in 29/485; do not delete the sense merely because its Infectum example is ambiguous.

Copied gməlš- with lost w, lušla, expanded lwəššanne and malwaṣto unchanged. Infectum-wa gives habitual wearing; existing III Infectum-wa gives unrealised obligation. No invented paradigm forms were added.
Most Jan evidence is interview recollection of habitual clothing, not exclusively written literary prose. I Infectum-wa is already filled by round 1, so repeated garment catalogues are not re-added.

III Infectum-wa gains explicit wearer/garment contrasts. I lwišo with a copula can describe the dressed wearer, not only a garment patient; this supports the Detransitive state interpretation proposed in round 1.

Retain new III Preterit-wa malwašwolən provisionally and distinguish it from malwəšiwolxu/malwəšinawolle Infectum-wa. Surface ləwšituwo in a habitual clothing question is corrected to Infectum-wa rather than using English tense as morphology.

The baptism pair kməlwəš / kləwašla provisionally contrasts Detransitive Infectum with I ko-Preterit. Baptism is b-marked at 4859, not a bare garment object. No new baptism sense is inferred from translation.

Glossary searches dayroyuṯo and nošuṯo found no existing lwš idiom. The new monastic-life phrase is listed as a collocation; ordinary monk clothing and possible priest-status ellipsis are not split into extra numbered senses.
One compact record, Jan 1.23/1218, lacks its verse. Its reader analysis cannot be independently checked; no example or semantic inference rests on it.
Do lwošo and təlwišo belong in Nomen Actionis or the team's Infinitiv paradigm, and can either be called Detransitive from form alone?
Does MAC NI death and newlyweds/12 lwəšlele show stem I dressing another person, a subject switch, or omitted mal-? Confirm before adding a sense.
In PrS 43/28 Kmalwašše ... la tre, is -še a recipient object or exceptional plural wearer form? Keep existing III.2 pending confirmation.
Reconcile old prs 2/3 with PrS 1/15, prs 24/25 with PrS 10/48, prs 110/31 with PrS 40/64, and prs 121/27 with PrS 43/28.
Verify Talay 1/75 Malwaššalli against existing LB75 malwaššal-le, and the two 81/122 gmalawšətwayle against existing -li; these are source/entry differences, not automatically copying errors.
What are the suffixes in lwəššanne and kmalwašlene? Is MAC NE Famine/53 lowašwayle generic singular or reduced plural?
At PrS 18/52, are the fingers coated with silver or magically restored as silver fingers? At 26/163, confirm malwašto beside malwišto.
87/126 has explicitly partial translation alignment; it is not quoted as a new example.
Confirm -wo-lən in lwəšwolən (975) and malwašwolən (4435), including which participants are agents and recipients. Confirm ko-Preterit segmentation of kləwašla (4859).
In Jan 2.31/5141 who clothes whom? Feminine i ruḥo qadišo and lwəšše do not justify the reader participant assignment without confirmation; the supplied English chooses an interpretation.
At 5600 is kuhne a result predicate, an omitted priestly garment, or a conventional phrase for entering office? Is dayroyo in 3422 analogous?
In candle making at 1575 does lowəš have an understood candle/wick subject, and is the coating construction ordinary I.1 or a distinct intrans. subsense?
Supply the missing full verse for the compact Jan 1.23/1218 record before treating its III analysis as checked.
Correct translation: 'Eigenturn' → 'Eigentum'
rationale: The German noun is 'Eigentum'. 'Eigenturn' is an evident rn/m transcription error, also present in the supplied corpus translation; it is not a legitimate spelling.

summary: Correct translation: 'säubere mit die Fingernägel' → 'säubere mir die Fingernägel'
